guard: the launch arms the event plane, a grant never does, an armed launch with no workspace root refuses instead of putting the write-ahead log somewhere no later start looks, and the connector DECLARES the event plane so an armed launch is not refused at the door
why: THIS SUITE EXISTS BECAUSE THE WIRING WAS DEAD AND EVERY OTHER SUITE WAS GREEN. The mapper and
the source were complete and correct, their two suites passed, eight mutations killed, and the
connector still could not have published a single frame in production: the launch path never set
COTAL_EVENTS, so the plugin never built an emitter. A suite that drives a component directly
cannot tell you whether a real entry point reaches it, and this is the cell set that answers the
second question rather than the first.
A1 is the arm itself. A2 is the refusal that keeps the write-ahead log out of the launch cwd,
where a later start would never look for it and would republish an already-published thread as
virgin. Both anchors are pure code.
A3 is the gate ABOVE buildLaunch and the one a live spawn hits first. The CLI and the manager both
refuse an armed launch whose connector does not implement `eventChannel`. This connector held a
complete emitter, armed it correctly, killed every mutation registered against it, and still exited
1 on a real `cotal spawn --events`, because it never declared that it emits. The cell compares the
declared channel to core's derivation BY VALUE: a method that merely exists is one more predicate
proved against itself and says nothing about the grant and the subject being one string.
